title: Tissue Protein Extraction Using Urea-based Buffer and Bead Mill Homogenizers
author: J P Rose

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Freshly prepare 10 mL of lysis buffer and keep cold using the following composition:

substeps.instruction: Add 2 mL of 200 mM TEAB, pH 8 (1 M)
Add 1 mL of 3 mM Nicotinamide (30 mM)
Add 150 µL of 75 mM Sodium chloride (5 M)
Add 100 µL of 1x HALT protease/phosphatase single-use inhibitor cocktail (100x)
Add 2 µL of 1 μM Trichostatin A (5 mM)
Bring to final volume with HPLC-grade water

steps.title: Prepare Homogenizer Adaptors
steps.instruction: Chill the adaptor sets of the bead mill homogenizer at -20°C.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: On dry ice, prepare the tissue specimen for homogenization.

substeps.instruction: Add the tissue specimen to a 2-mL microcentrifuge tube compatible with the bead mill homogenizer
Place the metallic bead into the tube
Add 500 µL of cold lysis buffer (add more if necessary to cover the tissue specimen)

steps.title: Homogenize Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize the samples using the bead mill homogenizer.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes in prechilled homogenizer adaptor sets, ensuring tubes are balanced between the two adaptors
Homogenize for 2 cycles at 24 Hz for 2 min each
If tissue is not fully homogenized: spin samples briefly, transfer lysate to a clean 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube, add additional lysis buffer, and repeat homogenization

steps.title: Recover Homogenized Lysate
steps.instruction: Remove the bead and collect the lysate.

substeps.instruction: Remove the bead with a tweezer
Rinse tweezers between samples with milliQ water, then HPLC-grade methanol, and dry with a delicate task wiper
Transfer the homogenized lysate into a clean 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube (or combine lysates if needed), avoiding bubbles and the separated fat layer

steps.title: Clear the Lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenized lysate at 15,700 x g for 15 min at 4°C.

steps.title: Collect Soluble Proteins
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (clear lysate containing soluble proteins) to a clean 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tube, carefully avoiding any liquid fat layer on top and debris at the bottom.

steps.title: Quantify Protein Concentration
steps.instruction: Determine the protein concentration of the clear lysate using a bicinchoninic acid (BCA) protein assay.

substeps.instruction: Use a proper dilution, typically 1:20 - 1:200 depending on the tissue type
Based on BCA results, transfer an aliquot of the sample into a clean 2-mL microcentrifuge tube for subsequent proteolytic digestion
